messages.subject: Re: different facet_plot panel widths
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gehoon and Ollie

I was able to do this with the grid and gtable package.

I got this from the following stack overflow thread:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49110877/how-to-adjust-facet-size-manually

I used Ollie's code as an example. see below

library(ggtree)
library(reshape2)

set.seed(123)
tree <- rtree(30)

# plot tree
p <- ggtree(tree, branch.length = "none") +
  geom_tiplab()

# make structure-like data
a <- runif(30, 0,1)
b <- 1 - a
df <- data.frame(tree$tip.label, a, b)
df <- melt(df, id = "tree.tip.label")

# plot tree with structure data

p2 <- facet_plot(p + xlim_tree(8), panel = 'bar', data = df, geom = geom_barh,

           mapping = aes(x = value, fill = as.factor(variable)), width = 0.7, stat='identity')

# load the packaged
library(grid)
library(gtable)

gt = ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p2))
gtable_show_layout(gt) # will show you the layout - very handy function
gt # see plot layout in table format
gt$layout$l[grep('panel-2', gt$layout$name)] # you want to find the column specific to panel-2
gt$widths[7] = 0.5*gt$widths[7] # in this case it was colmun 7 - reduce the width by a half
grid.draw(gt) # plot with grid draw

Hope it works for you!

Cheers

Pete

messages.subject: How to use data option in geom_tippoint?
messages.subject_clean: How to use data option in geom_tippoint?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Is it possible to highlight a subset of points using geom_tippoint?

In the following code, I want to to highlight t1, t2 in red and t2, t3 in blue.
But R prompts this error: "Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (5): node, subset, color, x, y".

Is there a way to use the option `data` in geom_tippoint so that I can highlight multiple subsets of tip points?

Thanks.

library(ggtree)

tree <- rtree(3) ## this create 3 tips: "t1" "t3" "t2"
d1 <- data.frame(node = c("t1", "t2"), color="red", size = 3, alpha = .8)
d1
d2 <- data.frame(node = c("t2", "t3"), color = "blue", size = 10, alpha = .2)
d2

p <- ggtree(tree)
p <- p +
  geom_tippoint(d1, color="red", size=3, alpha = .8) +
  geom_tippoint(d2, color="blue", size=10, alpha = .2)

print(p)
# Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (5): node, subset, color, x, y

messages.subject: Really aligning to the right tip labels of different lengths, with both align=T and hjust=1
messages.subject_clean: Really aligning to the right tip labels of different lengths, with both align=T and hjust=1
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

It seems it is not possible to really right-align the text of the labels of the tips when these labels have different text lengths. I don't want them at the tips, but all aligned, so I use align=T inside my call to geom_tiplab(). I also want the text itself to be right-aligned, so I use hjust=1, a.k.a hjust="right". But then I get the tree displayed in the attached SVG file: the labels are all right_aligned, ok, but I would like to move them a bit to the right so that they are not overlapping the end of the branch. Therefore I would like to further use a nudge_x=... argument, but it's impossible because it conflicts with something else:

Error in geom_segment2(mapping = segment_mapping, linetype = linetype,  :
  formal argument "nudge_x" matched by multiple actual arguments

I am running R version 3.5.0, with ggplot2 3.0.0 and ggtree 1.12.7. Can someone help me, please? Many thanks!

messages.body_plain:
I post this because I am facing the same problem: I want to change the text of the label (not the font, the face, the colour, etc: the text itself) of the leftmost panel which is automatically called "Tree" by ggtree. As far as I understand, and contrary to what is posted below, the "theme" thing of ggplot2 only allows to change the appearance of the panel header, not the text of the panel title itself... So how to go about that?

Many thanks,
   JB
